artifact_exists.ask: Is there an artifact at all — a repo, a deployed app, or a video of it running?
artifact_exists.settles_with: a repository, deployment or store listing we can resolve

build_is_real.ask: Is the code a real build (source tree, setup steps, non-trivial size) rather than a stub or zip?
build_is_real.settles_with: a readable source tree (a repo link, then `python3 pipeline/repo_verify.py`)

limits_disclosed.ask: Did they state what does not work, or where it fails?
limits_disclosed.settles_with: a statement of what the system itself cannot do (accuracy, coverage, privacy, failure modes)

numbers_add_up.ask: Do their metrics have a denominator, and is the arithmetic internally consistent?
numbers_add_up.settles_with: a denominator and baseline for the headline figure, or the raw log behind it

stack_consistency.ask: Does the repo's language/file mix match the stack they described?
stack_consistency.settles_with: a repository to compare the declared stack against

test_or_eval_evidence.ask: Any test suite, eval harness, or measured benchmark we can see?
test_or_eval_evidence.settles_with: a published eval table, harness or CI run link with a case count

policy: soundness and worth are never combined into one score
a verdict is a function of the evidence ledger, never typed by hand
unverifiable means no public evidence either way; it is not an accusation
records that cannot be supported stay in the pool, they are not deleted

verdicts.duplicate: Merged into an equivalent record (same submission or same-team resubmission).
verdicts.sound-with-caveats: Core mechanism verified; named gaps remain, listed as unknowns.
verdicts.strong: All load-bearing claims check out against artifacts; detail is sufficient to build from.
verdicts.thin: Not enough public evidence to certify either way — stays in the pool, never in the catalog.
verdicts.unsound: Load-bearing claim contradicted by evidence, or no artifact at all behind the pitch.

worth.breakthrough: Reframes a category; the mechanism outlives the project.
worth.niche: Correct and useful for a specific, smaller audience.
worth.strong: Genuine wedge, clearly better than the obvious alternative.
worth.tired: Competently built; the world already has five of these.
